question.text: A Cat III AIF launched by Ms. Radhika Rao has the following investor profile. Which of the following BREACHES SEBI (AIF) Regulations? (Corpus: INR 22 crore; 20 non-accredited investors.)

answer.text: One employee of the manager commits INR 30 lakh
One non-accredited HNI commits INR 50 lakh
One accredited investor commits INR 5 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: Minimum investment per investor in an AIF is INR 1 crore (for non-employee/non-director and non-accredited investors). Employees and directors of the manager can invest a minimum of INR 25 lakh. Accredited investors are exempt from the INR 1 crore floor under the accredited-investor framework. A non-accredited HNI committing only INR 50 lakh therefore violates the INR 1 crore minimum. The Trap: Option A matches the INR 1 crore floor exactly — compliant. Option B is INR 30 lakh by an employee — above the INR 25 lakh employee/director floor, compliant. Option D is an accredited investor — the INR 1 crore floor does not apply. Only C breaches. Note: Per the workbook (page 105), the INR 1 crore minimum, the INR 25 lakh employee/director exception, and the accredited-investor exemption together define the ticket-size compliance check.
